newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday, with most repo rates up on stronger fund demand due to three new Shanghai A share listings on Wednesday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract soared to 17.00 percent from last Friday's 3.04 percent.
Total turnover rose to nearly ten million lots from 7.70 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The rally on the domestic A share market attracted many funds from treasury bonds, with most repo rates pushed up by heavy institutional buying," said a local trader.
Three companies, Xinhua Metal Industrial Co, Si Sha Co. and Lu Yin Industrial (Group) Co. will make their market debuts in Shanghai on Wednesday.
"The new listings also caused a surge of early-maturing rates, with many institutions beginning to withdraw funds today," said a second trader.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down, mainly because investors were less interested in speculating on spot contracts, and trading volume shrank due to weaker market sentiment, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended down at 115.81 yuan from 116.09 yuan last Friday. Turnover fell to 570 million yuan from 820 million.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market shrank to 882,847 lots from 1.26 million lots.
"Selling of the most active ten-year contract increased," a trader said. "Some institutions liquidated their positions on rumours of more restrictions on spot market trading."
Traders expect volume to remain thin in the next few trading days.
